summary: Shinjo Suguro was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1945–1948, earning a doctorate by 1987). He held posts at Rissho University, including associate director in 1980 and professor emeritus (~1996–2004).

Shinjosei Mochizuki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1920–1923) and Kyoto University (~1923–1926), and later held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University.

Shinkai Sugawara was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Waseda University (until 1951) and Taisho University (doctorate, 1991). He held a post at Waseda University, becoming professor emeritus by 1972.

A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Murakami studied at Tohoku University under Nobuo Kumagai, Ensho Kanakura, Ryūjō Yamada, and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as professor (~1975–1996) and professor emeritus at Tohoku University, and held a post at Seiwa Gakuen College.

Shinko Nakai specialized in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. After studying at Kyoto Prefectural University (~1962–1966), he served as professor emeritus and former president during his career at Bukkyo University (~1978–2014).

Mochizuki studied under Tokuo Jonobe and at Bukkyo University, Jōdo Shūgaku Honkō, and the University of Tokyo. He served as president of Shukyo University (1914–1928) and as professor, dean, and library director at Taisho University (~1926–1942).

Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied under Charles Hallisey as her doctoral supervisor, Mark Csikszentmihalyi in 2000, and Robert Bickner as her academic adviser.
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning a PhD from Nagoya University in 1995, Yamaguchi held a post as professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Shinsho Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo (~1936–1959) and was a professor at Toyo University (~1924) and Kokugakuin University.

Kitano, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied under supervisor Kazunobu Matsuda. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and as a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).
Shinten Sakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Shindo Shiraishi. He later held a post at Koyasan University (attested 1959).

Shinya Mano works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Mano was a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2015–2019) and a research associate at SOAS University of London (attested 2019).

Shinya Moriyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed graduate degrees at the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998) and the University of Vienna (~2001–2006) and held a post at Shinshu University (~2009).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, Matsumoto studied at Komazawa and Tokyo universities under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He held posts at Komazawa University from 1982 to 2020 and was a visiting professor at Chicago in 2001.

Shiv Nath Sharma worked in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1947), and as a professor at St. Andrew's College, Gorakhpur (attested 1973).

Joshi was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard, Shankashastri Marulkar, and Maheshwarshastri Joshi. He served as professor and director at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1957–1986) and department head at Deccan College (~1987–1996).

Sasaki is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, Bukkyo University, and under Jikido Takasaki. He has served at Hanazono University as lecturer (1990), associate professor (1992), and professor of Indian Buddhism (2002).

Pines worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, studying at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Berlin (1926–1934). He taught at the University of Paris and Institut d'histoire des sciences (1937–1939), and served as philosophy professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1952–1990).

Shmuel Sambursky worked in philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Königsberg (~1921–1923) and the University of Berlin (~1923–1924), and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1928–1970).
Shobha Rani Dash works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Dash served as an open-recruitment researcher at Ryukoku University in 2010 and as a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012).
